lesson.text: Quick memory: in computing, what does a loop do? (It repeats steps.) Music can loop too!
A music loop is a short pattern that repeats again and again. Musicians call a repeating pattern an ostinato.
Start with a rhythm loop of 4 beats, like ta, ti-ti, ta, rest. Repeat it, and it becomes a groove.
Add a melody loop: choose a few notes, like C, E and G, and put them in a pattern. Repeat it.
Composers make choices: which notes, how long, in what order, fast or slow, loud or quiet. Change one thing and listen to how it sounds.
Layers: one friend claps the rhythm loop while another sings or plays the melody loop on top. Together they make a piece.
Write your loop down so you can play it again: ta, ti-ti and rest for the rhythm, and note names for the tune.
Try it in the world: build a loop in your world with blocks, one colour for each note. Walk along it singing each note, and when you reach the end, go back to the start!

exercises.explain: A music loop is a short pattern that repeats again and again.

exercises.hint: Listen for the same pattern coming again.
exercises.explain: True: the same 4 beats come twice.

exercises.prompt: Listen. How many times does the pattern play?
exercises.hint: Count each time the lowest note starts the pattern again.
exercises.explain: The three notes go round 3 times.

exercises.prompt: Listen to the loop, then copy one time round it in the boxes.
exercises.hint: Each beat has two boxes. ta: a clap in the first box. ti-ti: claps in both. A rest: no clap at all.
exercises.explain: One time round is ta, ti-ti: claps in boxes 1, 3 and 4.

exercises.prompt: Listen to this loop, then copy one time round in the boxes.
exercises.hint: Each beat has two boxes. ta: a clap in the first box. ti-ti: claps in both. A rest: no clap at all.
exercises.explain: One time round is ti-ti, ta: claps in boxes 1, 2 and 3.

exercises.prompt: Listen to the loop, then copy one time round: four beats, two boxes each.
exercises.hint: Each beat has two boxes. ta: a clap in the first box. ti-ti: claps in both. A rest: no clap at all.
exercises.explain: One time round is ta, ti-ti, ta, rest: claps in boxes 1, 3, 4 and 5.

choices: a pattern that repeats again and again
the last note of a song
exercises.explain: An ostinato is a musical pattern that repeats again and again, like a loop.

exercises.prompt: Listen. How many times does “ti-ti, ta” come?
exercises.hint: Count each ti-ti, ta as you listen.
exercises.explain: ti-ti, ta comes 3 times: the loop repeats 3 times.

exercises.hint: Listen to the first two notes: which is higher?
exercises.explain: G then E: a higher note, then a lower one, again and again.

exercises.prompt: Zara's loop is ta, ta, ti-ti. How many claps does it have each time round?
exercises.hint: ta is one clap, ti-ti is two.

exercises.prompt: A loop of 4 beats plays 5 times. How many beats is that altogether?
exercises.hint: Each time round is 4 beats. How many beats in 5 times round?

exercises.prompt: Listen. Is this tune a loop that repeats?
exercises.hint: Does any part come round again?
exercises.explain: False: every note is new, going up and up. A loop repeats its pattern.

exercises.prompt: Listen. Which rhythm is the loop?
exercises.hint: Listen as often as you like. Tap along, or say the rhythm quietly as you listen.
exercises.explain: The loop is ta, ta, ti-ti, rest, played twice.

exercises.prompt: You want your loop to sound calmer. What could you change?
exercises.explain: Slower and quieter makes a loop feel calmer.

exercises.prompt: Put the steps of composing in order.
exercises.hint: You can't choose before you try.
exercises.explain: Try ideas, choose your favourite, practise it, then perform it.

exercises.prompt: Listen. Which picture shows one time round the loop?
exercises.hint: Draw the tune in the air with your finger as you listen: up for higher notes, down for lower ones.
exercises.explain: Each time round goes up: C, E, G.

exercises.prompt: A rhythm loop and a melody loop played together are called layers.
exercises.hint: Remember the lesson card about friends playing together.
exercises.explain: True: one on top of another, like layers of a cake.

exercises.prompt: Listen. The loop is ta, ti-ti. How many claps are there altogether?
exercises.hint: Count the claps in one loop, then how many times it plays.
exercises.explain: ta, ti-ti is 1 + 2 = 3 claps, and it plays 3 times: 3 × 3 = 9 claps.
